items.text: Write What the UI Should Look Like

audio.text: React uses a declarative style, meaning you describe what the user interface should appear as for any given state, and React handles the updates efficiently.

scenes.title: Component Tree
scenes.subtitle: Visualizing UI as Nested Components
scenes.imagePrompt: A calm green background with a simple tree diagram of nested rectangles labeled Component, illustrating React component hierarchy

audio.text: React components are the building blocks of your application. Each component encapsulates its own logic and UI, allowing you to compose complex interfaces from small, reusable pieces.

Instead of manipulating the real browser DOM directly, React maintains a lightweight virtual representation. When state changes, it calculates the minimal set of updates and applies them to the actual DOM, boosting performance.
React introduces JSX, a syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like tags inside JavaScript. This makes component templates clearer and more maintainable.
In summary, React is a declarative library that uses components, a virtual DOM, and JSX to make building dynamic web interfaces efficient and maintainable.
